news.headline: PSX Closing Bell: A Touch of Red - KSE-100 confirmed Thursday close down 495.00 points (-0.28%)
news.summary: Thursday session (this checkpoint), from Wednesday's confirmed close of 176,042.99: KSE-100 settled at 175,547.98, down 495.00 points (-0.28%), per Mettis Global's 'PSX Closing Bell: A Touch of Red' (mettisglobal.news/latest) and corroborated by Express Tribune ('PSX falls 495 points as US-Iran tensions overshadow market') and PSX's own DPS indices page (captured Jul 30, 2026 3:50pm PKT, showing the same 175,547.98 level and -495.00-point move). Mettis attributes the session to persistent selling pressure in key sectors amid continued uncertainty over regional geopolitical tensions; oil & gas, cement and investment-bank names cited as laggards, fertiliser and commercial-bank names cited as relatively supportive. A modest continuation of the Middle East-tension-driven risk-off pattern already logged this cycle at higher impact; logged as impact 2 (background, sub-1% single-session move) for the index-level print.

news.headline: SCRA balance falls Rs82m to Rs27.3bn; rupee settles at Rs277.81/USD; Tasdeeq IPO floor price set at Rs1.90; PM orders crackdown on tax evaders
news.summary: Per Mettis Global's latest-news feed (mettisglobal.news/latest, checked 2026-07-30): the Special Convertible Rupee Account (SCRA) balance fell Rs82m to Rs27.3bn; the rupee posted a slight gain to settle at Rs277.81/USD in the interbank market; Tasdeeq's IPO floor price was set at Rs1.90/share (not a universe constituent); and the Prime Minister ordered a crackdown on tax evaders and the informal economy. Routine/background administrative and macro items, no PSX-ticker-level figures disclosed beyond the aggregate rupee/SCRA prints already consistent in kind with prior entries this newslog; logged as impact 1 (routine/administrative).

news.headline: Govt hikes petrol by Re1.09, HSD by Rs2.42 per litre
news.summary: Published Jul 30, 2026 11:47pm PKT: government raised ex-depot fuel prices - petrol +Re1.09 to Rs336.15/litre (from Rs335.06), HSD +Rs2.42 to Rs393.04/litre (from Rs390.62). Mettis's article states an 'Effective Date: July 31, 2026'; a separate ARY News report on the same hike described it as effective August 1, 2026 - the two sources disagree on the effective date and both are quoted here as found, unreconciled. Magnitude is far smaller than the Jul 11, 2026 hike (petrol +Rs13.18, HSD +Rs13.80, logged at impact 4); logged as impact 2 (minor, routine ex-depot price revision) per desk scale, with read-through for OMC (PSO) and refiners (ATRL, NRL, PRL).

news.headline: Petroleum pricing panel backs phased deregulation
news.summary: Published Jul 30, 2026 11:58pm PKT: the Prime Minister's Committee on Petroleum Pricing Reforms endorsed a phased move toward deregulation of petroleum pricing; no implementation timeline, specific mechanism, or affected-company figures disclosed in the source reviewed. Logged as impact 3 (notable, sector-relevant policy direction) pending confirmation of a formal implementation plan in a follow-up cycle; tagged to OMC (PSO, APL, CNERGY) and refiner (ATRL, NRL, PRL) constituents as the direct sector beneficiaries/exposures of any future pricing deregulation.

news.headline: PTCL board approves binding offer for majority stake acquisition
news.summary: Published Jul 31, 2026 10:42am PKT: PTCL's (PSX: PTC) board of directors approved a binding offer for the acquisition of a majority stake in an unnamed target company; the target's identity, purchase price and stake percentage were not disclosed in the source reviewed. Logged as impact 4 (major contract/M&A action) per desk news-impact criteria (Rule 10) despite undisclosed terms, given board-level approval of a binding acquisition offer; escalation flagged. Target identity and transaction value to be confirmed in a follow-up cycle.

news.headline: Maple Leaf Cement (MLCF) FY26 profit rises 9% to Rs12.56bn
news.summary: Published Jul 31, 2026 9:44am PKT: Maple Leaf Cement Factory Limited (PSX: MLCF) reported FY2026 (year ended June 30, 2026) net profit of Rs12.56bn, up 9% YoY from Rs11.50bn; EPS Rs11.34, up 3.28% YoY from Rs10.98; revenue rose 24% YoY to Rs85.15bn. No dividend disclosed in the source reviewed. This follows the Jul 30, 2026 board-meeting notice already logged this newslog (impact 1, 'no new results filed as of this check'); results have now been filed. Logged as impact 3 (notable, results date; modest in-line growth, not a surprise, no dividend) for this core-tier constituent.

news.headline: MLCF clears Rs2bn working capital facilities for KTML, MLCL
news.summary: Published Jul 31, 2026 10:22am PKT: Maple Leaf Cement's (MLCF) board approved extending Rs2bn working capital facilities each to Kohinoor Textile Mills Limited (KTML) and Maple Leaf Capital Limited (MLCL), described as a reciprocal intercompany treasury/financing arrangement; no interest rate, tenor, or further transaction detail disclosed in the source reviewed. Routine intercompany working-capital financing despite the Rs2bn-per-facility size; logged as impact 2 (minor company item) for MLCF and KTML.

news.headline: Engro Fertilizers (EFERT) 2QCY26 net profit falls 32% YoY to Rs3.8bn (EPS Rs2.85); DPS filing shows conflicting Rs3.11bn/EPS2.33
news.summary: Express Tribune (geopolitics-oil-spike-drag-psx-down, checked 2026-07-31) reported verbatim: 'EFERT reported 2QCY26 net profit of Rs3.8 billion (EPS Rs2.85), down 32% year-on-year.' A separate same-day check of EFERT's PSX Data Portal (DPS) company page shows its latest filing (dated Jul 30, 2026, for the six months ended June 30, 2026) carrying a Q2 2026 Profit after Taxation of Rs3,110,901 thousand and EPS of 2.33 - materially different from the Tribune-quoted Rs3.8bn/EPS2.85 figures. Both figures are reported here as found, unreconciled; no third source was located this cycle to corroborate either reading, and no dividend figure was confirmed in either source. First EFERT entry in this newslog. Logged as impact 4 (earnings surprise - a 32% YoY profit decline per the Tribune figure) per desk news-impact criteria (Rule 10) pending reconciliation of the conflicting PAT/EPS figures in a follow-up cycle; escalation flagged.

news.headline: Bank Alfalah (BAFL) Q2 2026 profit resolves prior unconfirmed flag - PAT approx. Rs10bn (EPS Rs3.22), up 27% YoY / 7.6% QoQ
news.summary: Express Tribune (geopolitics-oil-spike-drag-psx-down, checked 2026-07-31) reported verbatim: 'Bank Alfalah posted profit after tax of Rs10 billion (EPS Rs3.22) for the second quarter, up 27% year-on-year and 7.6% quarter-on-quarter.' A same-day re-check of BAFL's PSX Data Portal (DPS) company page now shows the Jul 30, 2026 half-year filing carrying a Q2 2026 standalone Profit after Taxation of Rs10,200,532 thousand (EPS field marked N/A on the DPS page) - closely corroborating the Tribune-quoted approximately Rs10bn figure. This resolves the 2026-07-30 newslog entry that had explicitly withheld BAFL's Q2/H1 PAT and EPS as unconfirmed (that entry's DPS fetch had returned a PAT of Rs11,126,356 thousand, matching BAFL's already-confirmed Q1 2026 figure almost exactly and inconsistent with an analyst survey projecting a Q2 profit decline - that earlier read remains unreconciled and is not restated here). No dividend figure confirmed in either source this cycle. Logged as impact 3 (notable, results confirmation) for this core-tier bank.

news.headline: Askari Bank (AKBL) H1 2026 profit jumps 25% to Rs13.35bn, declares Rs2/share dividend
news.summary: Published by Mettis Global (mettisglobal.news, headline 'Askari Bank profit jumps 25% to Rs13bn, declares Rs2 dividend'): Askari Bank Limited (PSX: AKBL) reported H1 2026 (six months ended June 30, 2026) profit after tax of Rs13.35bn, up 25% YoY from Rs10.70bn in H1 2025; the board declared a cash dividend of Rs2.00 per share. A same-day check of AKBL's PSX Data Portal (DPS) company page shows a separate Q2 2026 standalone filing carrying a Profit after Taxation of Rs6,566,158 thousand (~Rs6.57bn) and EPS of 4.53, with no dividend figure displayed on the DPS page as fetched - both figures reported here as found, unreconciled; no third source located this cycle to reconcile the H1-vs-Q2 figures or confirm the dividend on DPS. Logged as impact 4 (dividend announcement + material earnings growth) per desk news-impact criteria (Rule 10); escalation flagged.

news.headline: PM Shehbaz reviews OGRA reform plan, orders quick rollout
news.summary: Per Mettis Global's latest-news feed (mettisglobal.news/latest, checked this cycle) and corroborated by wire coverage (Geo News, Suchtv, Aaj News, ProPakistani, Bloom Pakistan): Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif reviewed the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) reform plan and directed its quick, undelayed implementation, stating - per the quoted directive - that 'no negligence or delay' in the rollout 'will be tolerated,' aimed at promoting competition, transparency and investment in the energy sector. No new specific mechanism, timeline or company-level figures disclosed beyond the directive itself; this is a continuation/reiteration of the Ogra-reform item already logged this newslog (2026-07-28, Cabinet Committee on Energy approving Oil Refining Policy amendments, impact 4). Logged as impact 2 (reiteration of an already-flagged policy direction, no new concrete figures) per desk scale; tagged to OMC/refiner/gas-utility constituents as the sector exposed to any future Ogra reform.

news.headline: National Refinery (NRL) raises Rs10bn through first-ever Sukuk to fund working capital
news.summary: Published Jul 30-31, 2026: National Refinery Limited (PSX: NRL) raised Rs10 billion through its first-ever Sukuk issuance, marking the company's debut in Pakistan's capital-market debt segment. The instrument is a rated, unsecured, privately placed short-term Sukuk with a six-month tenor, priced at three-month KIBOR minus 10 basis points per annum, and has been assigned an A1 rating by PACRA. NRL said the Sukuk will serve as an alternative source of funding for its working-capital requirements. Logged as impact 3 (notable capital-markets milestone, first debt-market instrument for this core-tier refiner) - a financing action, not an earnings result; no dividend or profit figure attached to this filing.

news.headline: OMO Result: SBP injects Rs12.38tr into market via reverse repo and Shariah-compliant Modarabah
news.summary: Published Jul 31, 2026 3:10pm PKT: State Bank of Pakistan conducted Open Market Operations injecting a total of Rs12.38 trillion - Rs11.91 trillion via conventional reverse repo (7-day tranche Rs163.1bn at 11.54%; 17-day tranche Rs11.75tr at 11.51%) and Rs471bn via Shariah-compliant Modarabah-based reverse repo (7-day Rs71bn at 11.56%; 17-day Rs400bn at 11.52%). Routine periodic SBP liquidity-management operation, consistent in kind with prior OMO items already logged this newslog; no PSX-ticker-level figures disclosed. Logged as impact 1 (routine/administrative).
